# `--json` reference

<!-- Generated by "pnpm docs:generate" from packages/cli/src/contract.ts. Do not edit. -->

Every command takes `--json`. With it, a command prints one JSON document on standard output, and nothing else there, whatever happens: its own document, or `mediaplane.error/v1` when it stops before it can print its own, a usage error included. What is for people, such as `plex-login`'s link, goes to standard error. Only `--help` and `--version` print text.

- **Every document names its shape** in `schema` (`mediaplane.<name>/v1`), and says in `ok` whether the command could do what it was asked. The exit code mostly says the same, but not for three commands: `plan` prints `ok: true` and exits 2 when apply would change something; `drift` prints `ok: true` and exits 2 when it found drift, or couldn't check a resource or a secret; `vpn-check` prints `ok: true` and exits 1 when it finds a leak or the VPN down (its `verdict` says which). Every other command exits 0 when `ok` is true, and 1 when not: the [CLI reference](cli.md) lists the exit codes.
- **The shapes below are generated from the code,** and a test checks that the CLI prints exactly them. Each has a JSON Schema in [`json/`](json/), one file per document.
- **Within v1 a shape only grows.** A later release may add a field, or a value to a field's values (such as a new `wiring[].action`), and never changes what one means: that would be v2. So a script reads the fields it knows and ignores the others, and stops at a value it doesn't know, rather than guess what it means. The JSON Schema files describe this release's shapes exactly: validate against the files of the release you run.
- **No secret is ever in a document,** but for the password `credentials --reveal` asks for.
- **A diagnostic's `severity` says whether it stopped the command;** its `code` says what it is, and stays the same from release to release, while its message is for people and may change. Within v1 a release may add codes. These are the codes a script is most likely to act on:

  - `config.missing`: the home has no `stack.yaml`
  - `config.old-version`: `stack.yaml` is an older version, read in memory (a warning): `mediaplane migrate` rewrites it
  - `apply.locked`: another Mediaplane command holds `state/lock`; `drift.locked`, `keep.locked` and `migrate.locked` say the same of theirs. Run it again once the other is done
  - `apply.pull-failed`: an image could not be pulled, even after the retries, before anything was stopped: run apply again
  - `secrets.admin-password-lost`: the admin password Mediaplane generated went with `state/secrets.json` (a warning): apply generates another and sets it in each app
  - `bootstrap.needs-password`: an app's first-run setup is held, since the app has never had the admin password Mediaplane holds: the rebuilding a host runbook says what to do
  - `bootstrap.open-published`: an app runs published though its first-run setup isn't shown to be done (a warning): apply starts it again without its ports first
  - `rotate.no-plex`: `--rotate plex.token` on a stack without Plex
  - `keep.external`: with `managed_by: external`, keep wrote nothing in `stack.yaml` (a warning): add its `line` there
  - `keep.record`: keep couldn't forget the record of a resource it keeps as unmanaged: run keep again before the next apply
  - `credentials.not-yet`: there is no admin password yet: run apply first
  - `vpn-check.not-applied`: the stack hasn't been applied, so there is nothing to check yet

## `mediaplane.plan/v1`

What apply would change: `mediaplane plan --json`.

JSON Schema: [`json/plan.schema.json`](json/plan.schema.json)

- `schema` (`"mediaplane.plan/v1"`)
- `ok` (boolean): false when a diagnostic is an error: then nothing else is planned
- `changed` (boolean): apply would change something; plan exits 2 then, and 0 when not
- `files` (list of objects): the files apply writes
  - `path` (string): relative to the Mediaplane home, such as `generated/compose.yaml`
  - `status` (one of `create`, `update` or `unchanged`)
  - `diff` (string): a unified diff from the file on disk; empty when the file is unchanged, or holds secrets
  - `sensitive` (boolean, optional): it holds secrets: compared with the file on disk, never shown
  - `prestart` (boolean, optional): written once, before the app's first start, and never updated
- `containers` (list of objects): what Compose does to each service
  - `service` (string): the Compose service, such as sonarr
  - `action` (one of `create`, `recreate`, `start`, `restart`, `remove` or `unchanged`)
- `secrets` (object): names only, never values
  - `generate` (list of strings): the secrets apply generates, by name, such as `sonarr.apiKey`
  - `recover` (list of strings): the keys apply recovers from the apps' appdata, which `state/secrets.json` lacks
  - `restore` (list of strings): the keys apply puts back in their apps' own files, stopping each app first
- `unhealthy` (list of strings): running apps whose health check has not passed yet, such as `sonarr (unhealthy)`: apply waits for them
- `wiring` (list of objects): what apply does to each managed resource
  - `resource` (string): `<app>.<resource>`, or `<app>` alone for an app Mediaplane only checks
  - `action` (one of `create`, `update`, `adopt`, `unchanged`, `after-start`, `unknown` or `remove`): adopt: the app holds it as wanted, and Mediaplane records it; after-start: checked once its app runs; unknown: Mediaplane could not ask the app (`reason` says why); remove: Mediaplane made it, and the stack no longer wants it
  - `changes` (list of strings, optional): the managed fields and secrets that differ, by name
  - `reason` (string, optional): why it could not be checked
- `bootstrap` (list of objects): the first-run setups apply finishes
  - `app` (string): the app whose first-run setup apply finishes, such as jellyfin
  - `unpublished` (boolean): it starts with no published port until its setup is done
  - `again` (boolean, optional): present, and true, only when the setup signs in again with what you rotated (`--rotate plex.token`), published or not
- `drift` (list of objects): what changed in the apps outside Mediaplane since it applied them
  - `resource` (string): `<app>.<resource>`, or `<app>` for an app that refuses its key
  - `kind` (one of `field`, `missing`, `secret`, `key` or `left`): field: a managed field holds another value; missing: deleted in the app; secret: the app's own check refuses one of its secrets; key: an app refuses its own key, or a resource holds that key (`source`); left: Mediaplane made it, the stack no longer wants it, and the app still holds it
  - `field` (string, optional): the managed field, for `field`
  - `expected` (string, number or boolean, optional): the value apply sets
  - `applied` (string, number or boolean, optional): the value Mediaplane applied, when `stack.yaml` has changed it since
  - `actual` (string, number, boolean or null, optional): what the app holds; null when Mediaplane can't read it (`unreadable`)
  - `unreadable` (string, optional): the shape Mediaplane can't read the value in
  - `redacted` (boolean, optional): `actual` or `unreadable` held a secret, shown as `***`
  - `secret` (string, optional): the secret, or key, by name: never its value
  - `since` (string, optional): when drift found it, for a secret or key not checked again until apply sets it
  - `source` (string, optional): key: the app whose key the resource holds, which that app refuses
  - `stays` (string, optional): left: why apply leaves it in the app; without it, apply removes it
- `checks` (list of objects): how each secret of each resource was checked: names only
  - `resource` (string): `<app>.<resource>`
  - `secret` (string): the secret, by name
  - `verdict` (one of `passed`, `refused` or `unchecked`)
  - `reason` (string, optional): why it was not checked
  - `at` (string, optional): when drift last checked it, for a verdict taken from then rather than checked again
- `diagnostics` (list of objects): every error and warning, in the order found
  - `severity` (one of `error` or `warning`): an error stopped the command; a warning did not
  - `code` (string): what it is, such as `config.unknown-key`: stable, for scripts to act on; the message is for people and may change
  - `message` (string): what is wrong, for people
  - `path` (string, optional): where in `stack.yaml`, such as `apps.qbittorrent.vpn`
  - `hint` (string, optional): what to do about it

## `mediaplane.apply/v1`

What apply did: `mediaplane apply --yes --json`.

JSON Schema: [`json/apply.schema.json`](json/apply.schema.json)

- `schema` (`"mediaplane.apply/v1"`)
- `ok` (boolean): the apply succeeded, or there was nothing to change; apply exits 0 then
- `changed` (boolean): apply changed something on the host or in the apps
- `outcome` (one of `success`, `failed`, `no-changes`, `cancelled` or `invalid`): invalid: the plan failed, and nothing was changed; cancelled: nothing was changed
- `plan` (object): the plan apply followed
  - `files` (list of objects): the files apply writes
    - `path` (string): relative to the Mediaplane home, such as `generated/compose.yaml`
    - `status` (one of `create`, `update` or `unchanged`)
    - `diff` (string): a unified diff from the file on disk; empty when the file is unchanged, or holds secrets
    - `sensitive` (boolean, optional): it holds secrets: compared with the file on disk, never shown
    - `prestart` (boolean, optional): written once, before the app's first start, and never updated
  - `containers` (list of objects): what Compose does to each service
    - `service` (string): the Compose service, such as sonarr
    - `action` (one of `create`, `recreate`, `start`, `restart`, `remove` or `unchanged`)
  - `secrets` (object): names only, never values
    - `generate` (list of strings): the secrets apply generates, by name, such as `sonarr.apiKey`
    - `recover` (list of strings): the keys apply recovers from the apps' appdata, which `state/secrets.json` lacks
    - `restore` (list of strings): the keys apply puts back in their apps' own files, stopping each app first
  - `unhealthy` (list of strings): running apps whose health check has not passed yet, such as `sonarr (unhealthy)`: apply waits for them
  - `wiring` (list of objects): what apply does to each managed resource
    - `resource` (string): `<app>.<resource>`, or `<app>` alone for an app Mediaplane only checks
    - `action` (one of `create`, `update`, `adopt`, `unchanged`, `after-start`, `unknown` or `remove`): adopt: the app holds it as wanted, and Mediaplane records it; after-start: checked once its app runs; unknown: Mediaplane could not ask the app (`reason` says why); remove: Mediaplane made it, and the stack no longer wants it
    - `changes` (list of strings, optional): the managed fields and secrets that differ, by name
    - `reason` (string, optional): why it could not be checked
  - `bootstrap` (list of objects): the first-run setups apply finishes
    - `app` (string): the app whose first-run setup apply finishes, such as jellyfin
    - `unpublished` (boolean): it starts with no published port until its setup is done
    - `again` (boolean, optional): present, and true, only when the setup signs in again with what you rotated (`--rotate plex.token`), published or not
- `actions` (list of objects): each step's actions, in order
  - `step` (one of `keys`, `files`, `pull`, `ownership`, `start`, `bootstrap`, `wire` or `verify`)
  - `resource` (string, optional): the wire step names the resource, such as `sonarr.admin`
  - `result` (one of `done`, `failed` or `skipped`)
  - `detail` (string, optional): what it did, for people: a wire action says `created`, `updated`, `adopted`, `unchanged` or `removed`, and a skipped one why, such as why a planned removal stays; the first-run setup step says what it set up and published, and `signed in again to <app>`
  - `error` (string, optional): why it failed
- `recordId` (string or null): the change record written (`mediaplane history <id>`), or null
- `diagnostics` (list of objects): every error and warning, in the order found
  - `severity` (one of `error` or `warning`): an error stopped the command; a warning did not
  - `code` (string): what it is, such as `config.unknown-key`: stable, for scripts to act on; the message is for people and may change
  - `message` (string): what is wrong, for people
  - `path` (string, optional): where in `stack.yaml`, such as `apps.qbittorrent.vpn`
  - `hint` (string, optional): what to do about it

## `mediaplane.drift/v1`

What changed in the apps outside Mediaplane: `mediaplane drift --json`.

JSON Schema: [`json/drift.schema.json`](json/drift.schema.json)

- `schema` (`"mediaplane.drift/v1"`)
- `ok` (boolean): false when drift couldn't look: an error diagnostic says why
- `clear` (boolean): nothing drifted, and every resource and secret was checked: drift exits 0 then, and 2 when not
- `drift` (list of objects): what changed in the apps outside Mediaplane
  - `resource` (string): `<app>.<resource>`, or `<app>` for an app that refuses its key
  - `kind` (one of `field`, `missing`, `secret`, `key` or `left`): field: a managed field holds another value; missing: deleted in the app; secret: the app's own check refuses one of its secrets; key: an app refuses its own key, or a resource holds that key (`source`); left: Mediaplane made it, the stack no longer wants it, and the app still holds it
  - `field` (string, optional): the managed field, for `field`
  - `expected` (string, number or boolean, optional): the value apply sets
  - `applied` (string, number or boolean, optional): the value Mediaplane applied, when `stack.yaml` has changed it since
  - `actual` (string, number, boolean or null, optional): what the app holds; null when Mediaplane can't read it (`unreadable`)
  - `unreadable` (string, optional): the shape Mediaplane can't read the value in
  - `redacted` (boolean, optional): `actual` or `unreadable` held a secret, shown as `***`
  - `secret` (string, optional): the secret, or key, by name: never its value
  - `since` (string, optional): when drift found it, for a secret or key not checked again until apply sets it
  - `source` (string, optional): key: the app whose key the resource holds, which that app refuses
  - `stays` (string, optional): left: why apply leaves it in the app; without it, apply removes it
- `checks` (list of objects): how each secret was checked: names only
  - `resource` (string): `<app>.<resource>`
  - `secret` (string): the secret, by name
  - `verdict` (one of `passed`, `refused` or `unchecked`)
  - `reason` (string, optional): why it was not checked
  - `at` (string, optional): when drift last checked it, for a verdict taken from then rather than checked again
- `unchecked` (list of objects): the resources drift couldn't look at
  - `resource` (string): `<app>.<resource>`
  - `reason` (string): why
- `diagnostics` (list of objects): every error and warning, in the order found
  - `severity` (one of `error` or `warning`): an error stopped the command; a warning did not
  - `code` (string): what it is, such as `config.unknown-key`: stable, for scripts to act on; the message is for people and may change
  - `message` (string): what is wrong, for people
  - `path` (string, optional): where in `stack.yaml`, such as `apps.qbittorrent.vpn`
  - `hint` (string, optional): what to do about it

## `mediaplane.keep/v1`

What Keep mine kept: `mediaplane keep <path> --json`.

JSON Schema: [`json/keep.schema.json`](json/keep.schema.json)

- `schema` (`"mediaplane.keep/v1"`)
- `ok` (boolean): something was kept; keep exits 0 then
- `key` (string): the override key, or the app key (`<app>.<key>`), as asked
- `value` (string, number, boolean or null): the value kept, or `unmanaged` for a resource; null for an app's own key, which `state/secrets.json` keeps
- `holders` (list of strings, optional): an app's own key: the resources that hold the old one, which the next apply gives the kept one
- `line` (string, optional): the line under `overrides:` that keeps it, as written, or for you to add: present once keep got as far as the line
- `written` (boolean, optional): keep wrote `line` into `stack.yaml`; false with `managed_by: external` (a `keep.external` warning), or when it could not
- `diagnostics` (list of objects): every error and warning, in the order found
  - `severity` (one of `error` or `warning`): an error stopped the command; a warning did not
  - `code` (string): what it is, such as `config.unknown-key`: stable, for scripts to act on; the message is for people and may change
  - `message` (string): what is wrong, for people
  - `path` (string, optional): where in `stack.yaml`, such as `apps.qbittorrent.vpn`
  - `hint` (string, optional): what to do about it

## `mediaplane.migrate/v1`

What migrate did: `mediaplane migrate --json`.

JSON Schema: [`json/migrate.schema.json`](json/migrate.schema.json)

- `schema` (`"mediaplane.migrate/v1"`)
- `ok` (boolean): `stack.yaml` is now, or already was, the version this Mediaplane writes
- `from` (number, optional): the version `stack.yaml` was, when it could be read
- `to` (number): the version this Mediaplane writes
- `changed` (boolean): `stack.yaml` was rewritten
- `applied` (list of strings): what each migration step changed, in order
- `text` (string, optional): the file as it should be, when Mediaplane may not write it (`managed_by: external`)
- `diagnostics` (list of objects): every error and warning, in the order found
  - `severity` (one of `error` or `warning`): an error stopped the command; a warning did not
  - `code` (string): what it is, such as `config.unknown-key`: stable, for scripts to act on; the message is for people and may change
  - `message` (string): what is wrong, for people
  - `path` (string, optional): where in `stack.yaml`, such as `apps.qbittorrent.vpn`
  - `hint` (string, optional): what to do about it

## `mediaplane.status/v1`

Each app's container, and the last apply: `mediaplane status [app] --json`.

JSON Schema: [`json/status.schema.json`](json/status.schema.json)

- `schema` (`"mediaplane.status/v1"`)
- `ok` (`true`): true: the containers were listed
- `healthy` (boolean): there are containers, and every one is running and passes its health check
- `containers` (list of objects): the stack's containers, sorted by service
  - `service` (string): the Compose service
  - `state` (string): running, exited, created, …
  - `health` (string): healthy, unhealthy, starting, or empty with no health check
  - `published` (list of objects): where its ports are published on the host
    - `address` (string): the host address
    - `port` (number)
    - `protocol` (one of `tcp` or `udp`)
- `lastApply` (object or null): the last apply, or null if none has run
  - `id` (string): the change record, as `mediaplane history <id>` takes it
  - `startedAt` (string): when the apply started, in ISO 8601
  - `durationMs` (number): how long it took
  - `outcome` (one of `success` or `failed`)
  - `changes` (object): how much it changed
    - `files` (number): files written
    - `containers` (number): containers changed
    - `secrets` (number): secrets generated
    - `wiring` (number): resources the wire step changed in the apps
- `historyError` (string, optional): why the change history couldn't be read; the containers are listed all the same

## `mediaplane.history/v1`

The change records: `mediaplane history --json`.

JSON Schema: [`json/history.schema.json`](json/history.schema.json)

- `schema` (`"mediaplane.history/v1"`)
- `ok` (`true`): true: the records were listed
- `records` (list of objects): every change record, newest first
  - `id` (string): the change record, as `mediaplane history <id>` takes it
  - `startedAt` (string): when the apply started, in ISO 8601
  - `durationMs` (number): how long it took
  - `outcome` (one of `success` or `failed`)
  - `changes` (object): how much it changed
    - `files` (number): files written
    - `containers` (number): containers changed
    - `secrets` (number): secrets generated
    - `wiring` (number): resources the wire step changed in the apps
- `unreadable` (list of strings): the files in `state/history/` this Mediaplane can't read: a later release's, or damaged

## `mediaplane.change/v1`

One change record, as this release knows it: `mediaplane history <id> --json`. A later release's record shows only these fields; the rest stay in its file.

JSON Schema: [`json/change.schema.json`](json/change.schema.json)

- `schema` (`"mediaplane.change/v1"`)
- `id` (string matching `^\d{8}T\d{6}Z-[0-9a-f]{8}$`): the record, such as `20261009T094312Z-a1b2c3d4`
- `trigger` (`"cli"`)
- `startedAt` (string (an ISO 8601 date and time))
- `finishedAt` (string (an ISO 8601 date and time))
- `durationMs` (integer)
- `outcome` (one of `success` or `failed`)
- `stackSha256` (string matching `^[0-9a-f]{64}$`): the SHA-256 of `stack.yaml` as applied
- `plan` (object): the plan the apply followed, without its diffs
  - `files` (list of objects)
    - `path` (string): relative to the Mediaplane home
    - `status` (one of `create`, `update` or `unchanged`)
  - `containers` (list of objects)
    - `service` (string): the Compose service, such as sonarr
    - `action` (one of `create`, `recreate`, `start`, `restart`, `remove` or `unchanged`)
  - `secrets` (object): names only, never values
    - `generate` (list of strings): the secrets generated, by name
    - `recover` (list of strings, optional): the keys recovered from the apps' appdata
    - `restore` (list of strings, optional): the keys put back in their apps' own files
  - `wiring` (list of objects, optional)
    - `resource` (string): `<app>.<resource>`, or `<app>` alone for an app Mediaplane only checks
    - `action` (one of `create`, `update`, `adopt`, `unchanged`, `after-start`, `unknown` or `remove`): adopt: the app holds it as wanted, and Mediaplane records it; after-start: checked once its app runs; unknown: Mediaplane could not ask the app (`reason` says why); remove: Mediaplane made it, and the stack no longer wants it
    - `changes` (list of strings, optional): the managed fields and secrets that differ, by name
    - `reason` (string, optional): why it could not be checked
  - `bootstrap` (list of objects, optional)
    - `app` (string): the app whose first-run setup apply finishes, such as jellyfin
    - `unpublished` (boolean): it starts with no published port until its setup is done
    - `again` (boolean, optional): present, and true, only when the setup signs in again with what you rotated (`--rotate plex.token`), published or not
- `actions` (list of objects)
  - `step` (one of `keys`, `files`, `pull`, `ownership`, `start`, `bootstrap`, `wire` or `verify`)
  - `resource` (string, optional): the wire step names the resource, such as `sonarr.admin`
  - `result` (one of `done`, `failed` or `skipped`)
  - `detail` (string, optional): what it did, for people: a wire action says `created`, `updated`, `adopted`, `unchanged` or `removed`, and a skipped one why, such as why a planned removal stays; the first-run setup step says what it set up and published, and `signed in again to <app>`
  - `error` (string, optional): why it failed
- `ok` (`true`): true: the record was read

## `mediaplane.credentials/v1`

The shared admin login, and each app's web address: `mediaplane credentials [app] --json`.

JSON Schema: [`json/credentials.schema.json`](json/credentials.schema.json)

- `schema` (`"mediaplane.credentials/v1"`)
- `ok` (`true`): true: the login was found
- `username` (string): the shared admin user name
- `password` (string or null): the shared admin password with `--reveal`; null without it
- `passwordSource` (one of `generated` or `yours`): generated: Mediaplane's; yours: from `admin.password`
- `apps` (list of objects, each one of those below): each app with a web login
  - With `login` `"shared"`:
    - `app` (string): the app, such as sonarr
    - `name` (string): its name, such as Sonarr
    - `urls` (list of strings): where its web UI is published: one URL per address
    - `login` (`"shared"`): signs in with the shared admin
  - With `login` `"own"`:
    - `app` (string): the app, such as sonarr
    - `name` (string): its name, such as Sonarr
    - `urls` (list of strings): where its web UI is published: one URL per address
    - `login` (`"own"`): signs in with an account of its own
    - `account` (string): whose account, such as Plex
  - With `login` `"not-yet"`:
    - `app` (string): the app, such as sonarr
    - `name` (string): its name, such as Sonarr
    - `urls` (list of strings): where its web UI is published: one URL per address
    - `login` (`"not-yet"`): its login is still to come
    - `comingIn` (string): when it comes

## `mediaplane.vpn-check/v1`

Whether qBittorrent reaches the internet only through the VPN: `mediaplane vpn-check --json`.

JSON Schema: [`json/vpn-check.schema.json`](json/vpn-check.schema.json)

- `schema` (`"mediaplane.vpn-check/v1"`)
- `ok` (`true`): true: the check ran; verdict says what it found
- `verdict` (one of `pass`, `leak` or `down`): pass exits 0; leak and down exit 1
- `checks` (list of objects): each check, in order
  - `id` (one of `network`, `gluetun`, `control`, `control-key`, `route` or `egress`)
  - `status` (one of `ok`, `warning`, `down` or `leak`)
  - `message` (string): what it found, for people
  - `hint` (string, optional): what to do about it
- `egress` (object or null): the addresses compared; null with --no-egress
  - `url` (string): the IP-echo service asked
  - `vpn` (string or null): qBittorrent's address, or null
  - `host` (string or null): this host's address, or null
- `gluetunPublicIp` (string or null): the address Gluetun reports for itself, or null
- `failClosed` (boolean): qBittorrent was shown to be in Gluetun's network, and nothing can get out around the VPN

## `mediaplane.plex-login/v1`

Your Plex sign-in: `mediaplane plex-login --json`; the link goes to stderr.

JSON Schema: [`json/plex-login.schema.json`](json/plex-login.schema.json)

- `schema` (`"mediaplane.plex-login/v1"`)
- `ok` (`true`): true: a token that works is saved
- `saved` (string): the file the token is saved in: never the token
- `signedIn` (boolean): you signed in now; false when the saved token works already
- `replaced` (boolean): it replaced another token: run `apply --rotate plex.token` next

## `mediaplane.init/v1`

The starter `stack.yaml`: `mediaplane init --json`.

JSON Schema: [`json/init.schema.json`](json/init.schema.json)

- `schema` (`"mediaplane.init/v1"`)
- `ok` (`true`): true: stack.yaml was written
- `stackPath` (string): the `stack.yaml` written
- `next` (list of strings): what to do next, for people, in order

## `mediaplane.error/v1`

A command that stopped before it could print its own document: a usage error, a missing `stack.yaml` for credentials or vpn-check, Docker out of reach.

JSON Schema: [`json/error.schema.json`](json/error.schema.json)

- `schema` (`"mediaplane.error/v1"`)
- `ok` (`false`)
- `error` (object)
  - `message` (string): what went wrong, for people
  - `diagnostics` (list of objects, optional): the diagnostics that stopped the command, when it has them
    - `severity` (one of `error` or `warning`): an error stopped the command; a warning did not
    - `code` (string): what it is, such as `config.unknown-key`: stable, for scripts to act on; the message is for people and may change
    - `message` (string): what is wrong, for people
    - `path` (string, optional): where in `stack.yaml`, such as `apps.qbittorrent.vpn`
    - `hint` (string, optional): what to do about it
